ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and senior managers against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the New Zealand sanctions list maintained under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and the New Zealand Terrorist Designations Act 1999, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be risk-rated and subject to enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth and source of funds verification, adverse media checks, and enhanced transaction monitoring. For a medium-risk aviation spares trader under ISIC 4659, additional screening is required for counterparties, freight forwarders, and intermediaries against sanctions evasion typologies, dual-use export controls, and civil aviation authorities’ restricted party lists. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Registration and Name Reservation Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the English or Latin script, but Maori words, initials, numbers, and punctuation are permissible if clearly legible and not confusingly similar to an existing name. The New Zealand Companies Office applies a four-tier naming test: (1) identical or almost identical to an existing name, (2) names that suggest a relationship with a government agency, Crown entity, or registered charity, (3) names containing restricted words or phrases requiring approval from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Financial Markets Authority, or other relevant regulator, and (4) names that are offensive, objectionable, or likely to mislead the public. Phonetic equivalence and transliteration are evaluated against the standard New Zealand English pronunciation, including Maori language official names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant may file a formal appeal with the Registrar of Companies under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Registrar at the New Zealand Companies Office, setting out full legal grounds, any letters of consent from the regulator concerned, and evidence that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing name. The Registrar will review the appeal and issue a decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand within 28 days of the Registrar’s final decision, but the name reservation must be refreshed if it expires during the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox address is legally permissible for the Companies Office registered office requirement, provided the address is a physical location in New Zealand where service of documents can be effected and the company maintains a physical presence through its registered agent. However, for the purpose of GST registration and opening a business bank account with an authorized New Zealand bank, a virtual office alone will likely be rejected by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and banks, particularly for an aviation spares trading business under ISIC 4659, because the industry is expected to maintain an operational physical office, storage or inspection facility, or at least a documented commercial substance in New Zealand. The entity should therefore secure a physical registered office and, if practicable, a leased office or service arrangement with a licensed commercial agent to satisfy both the Companies Office and the due diligence expectations of correspondent banks.

observed_risk_factors: The business is classified as medium-risk enhanced by the AML/CFT classification.
The industry involves civil aviation parts, rotables, and avionics, which are sensitive high-value goods.
The entity is wholly owned by non-residents with no clear domestic operational history.
The registered office is the only New Zealand address presented to IRD and banks.
The company is expected to claim input tax credits for imported aviation inventory.
physical_inspection_likelihood.recommendation: Maintain a physical registered office and make available records, inventory access, and personnel in New Zealand. Prepare an on-site inspection response kit containing statutory registers, board resolutions, bank statements, and goods movement documentation to mitigate any unannounced visit by IRD, Companies Office, or the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (No 105 of 1993), particularly section 10 (prohibition on unregistered companies and incorporation), sections 12-14 (registered office and records), sections 15-19 (constitution), sections 51-59 (issue of shares and capital), sections 151-160 (appointment and powers of directors), section 180 (resolutions and meetings), and sections 189-215 (company records and annual return obligations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register and the Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a New Zealand Company under the Companies Act 1993 (online form filed through the Companies Office portal using RealMe authentication)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand companies have no statutory minimum paid-up capital. A company may be incorporated with no issued capital or a nominal share capital, and shares have no par value under the Companies Act 1993. No blocked escrow account is required. Shares may be issued for cash or non-cash consideration, and the board must pass a resolution approving the issue and be satisfied that the asset or benefit received as consideration is adequate and fairly measurable under section 58.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
AT A MEETING of the Board of Directors of NZ_LTD (the ‘Company’), held at the registered office of the Company on [Date of Meeting], the following directors were present and constituted a quorum: [Full Names of Initial Directors]. The Chair reported that the Company had been duly incorporated by the New Zealand Companies Office on [Date of Incorporation], holding Certificate of Incorporation number [NZBN Number], and that the Company is governed by the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution filed at incorporation. After deliberation, the Board unanimously RESOLVED as follows:

1. CONSTITUTION AND STATUTORY RECORDS: The Constitution of the Company, as registered with the Companies Office, is hereby ratified, approved, and adopted in full. The directors and officers of the Company are directed to maintain all statutory registers and records at the registered office in accordance with sections 189-215 of the Companies Act 1993, including the shareholders register, director and officer register, minutes of meetings, and financial records.

2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The allotment and subscription of shares of the Company, as recorded in the shareholders register, be and are hereby approved. The subscribers listed in the share register are confirmed as shareholders of the Company, subscribing for the number of shares set opposite their respective names, at the respective subscription consideration recorded in the register. The directors confirm that the consideration for each share issue is lawful, that the shares have been or will be recorded as fully paid or partly paid as marked in the register, and that no minimum capital escrow requirement exists under New Zealand law.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at [Physical Registered Office Address, New Zealand]. Such address shall be entered in the Companies Register and shall be the place where all statutory records and registers are kept and where notices and legal process may be served.

4. BANKING AUTHORISATION: [Name of Bank] is appointed as the principal banker of the Company. The Directors are authorized to open bank accounts, including operating, escrow, and trust accounts, using SWIFT wire and aviation escrow rails. The Managing Director and the Chief Financial Officer, or any two directors jointly, are hereby authorized to sign banking instructions, cheques, wire transfer requests, loan agreements, and all account documentation. The bank is entitled to rely on this resolution until written revocation is received.

5. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: The following officers be and are hereby appointed with authority appropriate to their offices: [Full Name] as Managing Director and chief executive officer; [Full Name] as Chief Financial Officer; [Full Name] as Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Compliance Officer; and [Full Name] as Company Secretary, if compatible with the Company’s governance structure. Each appointee is authorized to execute documents, instruct professional advisers, and represent the Company in respect of the ordinary administrative, regulatory, and commercial affairs of the Company.

6. AUTHORITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Each director and officer is directed to take all necessary steps to register for tax, obtain industrial and physical licensing, satisfy banking due diligence, and maintain corporate good standing. All actions taken prior to this resolution in connection with incorporation are hereby ratified and confirmed.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Companies Register online portal via RealMe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the New Zealand Companies Office online search facility and conduct a New Zealand Business Number and Companies Register name search for the exact proposed corporate name ‘NZ LTD’ and its structural variants, including ‘NZ LIMITED’ and ‘NZ LIMITED COMPANY’. Verify that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered and that the proposed name does not breach the restrictions in Part 3 of the Companies Act 1993 relating to names that are offensive, illegal, or likely to mislead. If the exact name is available, reserve it where the online workflow permits or proceed directly to incorporation using that name. Prepare at least three alternative acceptable names and record them in the application workspace for immediate substitution if the primary name is refused or objected to.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and transliteration variants
Alternative company names in order of preference
RealMe login credentials
New Zealand registered office address proposed for the entity
Completed name availability search output
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is flagged as indistinguishable from an existing name, select the next available alternative name and resubmit the search. If the name is objected to by a third party under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, file a written response and evidence of consent or goodwill, or amend the name to a non-conflicting variant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Governance Documents and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of NZ_LTD in consultation with the New Zealand Companies Office as filing registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution of NZ_LTD in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, or elect to rely on the default first schedule rules by adopting no separate constitution. Prepare the director consent forms signed by each proposed director, confirming capacity, eligibility, and acceptance of statutory duties, together with section 151 consents and any required disclosure of beneficial ownership. Identify all initial shareholders and their respective share allocations, ensuring the share structure is consistent with the proposed bank account, escrow, and aviation trade profile. Confirm that the proposed registered office is a physical street address in New Zealand and not a post office box. Execute all consents and dated corporate resolutions with original or electronic signatures acceptable under the Electronic Transactions Act 2002.
required_dossiers: Proposed constitution or express election to adopt default rules
Signed director consent forms under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993
Signed shareholder subscription and consent forms
Share allocation schedule
Proof of physical registered office address in New Zealand
AML/CFT beneficial ownership declaration for initial shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent is rejected or found defective, prepare corrected execution pages and disqualified-director declarations. If the registered office address is invalid, provide a substituted address before filing. Where the constitution is defective, amend the constitution before submission by written resolution of all consenting shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Submission of Incorporation Application and Government Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online Companies Register application service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register with the authenticated RealMe identity. Select ‘Register a Company’ and complete the online incorporation application by entering the proposed name, registered office physical address, postal address, directors, shareholders, share structure, and any filed constitution. Declare the intended business activity as wholesale distribution of surplus commercial aircraft rotables and avionics parts, classified under ISIC 4659 and NAICS 423860. Confirm that each proposed director has consented, that no undischarged bankrupt or disqualified person is appointed, and that the registered office is in New Zealand. Review all declarations and certifications, then submit the application and pay the official incorporation fee using a corporate or international payment card. Retain the payment receipt, application reference number, and confirmation screen as evidence of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Companies Office incorporation application
RealMe authenticated identity and authorization evidence
Signed director consent forms
Proposed constitution (if adopted)
Share structure and initial shareholder schedule
Registered office address authority
Payment receipt for official state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a Notice of Intention to Refuse Registration, submit a written response within the stated deadline explaining any discrepancy, correct the entry using the online amendment function, or withdraw and resubmit the application with the corrected data. If the payment is not accepted, use an alternative payment channel or remit payment before the provisional file expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN Activation and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Companies Office issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and activates the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The directors shall verify that the certificate is correctly issued in the exact legal name, review the NZBN record for accuracy, and update any preferences for electronic service. The Company must then apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number and determine whether it is required to register for GST, PAYE, and withholding tax. If annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZ$60,000, GST registration is mandatory; otherwise voluntary registration may still be appropriate for the aviation spares industry. Submit the bank introduction package comprising the certificate, directors’ identification, constitutional documents, and AML/CFT compliance records to the selected bank or banking intermediary.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation notice
Directors’ original or certified passports and proof of residential address
Constitution and first board resolution
Inland Revenue IRD number and GST registration application
Bank account due diligence and beneficial ownership forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a typographical error in the corporate name, apply immediately to the Companies Office for administrative correction. If the IRD number is delayed, escalate through the IRD business helpline and provide the NZBN and certificate of incorporation as cross-references. If the bank declines the account application due to enhanced due diligence, supplement with the completed statutory declaration, trade references, and aviation insurance certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of First Board Resolution, Officer Appointments and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD, in coordination with the Companies Office registrar and the appointed banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the formal first meeting of the Board prior to any business activity. Present the pro-forma first board resolution covering adoption of the constitution, ratification of share subscriptions, establishment of the registered office, appointment of statutory officers, and banking authorization. The Board must satisfy itself that the Company has adequate governance and AML/CFT controls for its Medium-Risk Enhanced aviation spares trading profile. Pass the resolution and enter into the minutes. After execution, file any director or officer changes with the Companies Office where the online register requires, update the shareholders register with the exact allotment, and open the corporate bank accounts, including escrow, SWIFT wire, and currency accounts, using the executed board resolution as the mandate.
required_dossiers: Executed pro-forma first board resolution
Minute of board meeting and quorum certificate
Registration certificate and NZBN
Share allotment register entries
Officer consent forms
Bank mandate and signatory signature cards
AML/CFT programme and compliance officer appointment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office rejects a director or officer filing due to incomplete forms, correct the declaration and refile immediately. If a bank signatory mandate is refused, revise the board resolution to reflect the bank’s required signature matrix and adopt a director’s certificate confirming authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Physical, Fire and Environmental Licensing Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority or city/district council, Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), Worksafe New Zealand, and the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the Company will maintain an actual warehouse, stockroom, office, or third-party logistics arrangement. For any physical storage premises used for surplus aircraft parts and avionics, confirm that the building has a current Building Warrant of Fitness, an approved Compliance Schedule, and a building consent for the intended storage use. If five or more persons are employed or hazardous chemicals are present, submit a Fire Evacuation Scheme to FENZ. If the site stores or handles any aviation fluids, oils, lithium batteries, solvents, or classified dangerous goods, obtain a Hazardous Substances Location Approval and comply with NZS 5433:2020 for transportable hazardous substances. Confirm with Worksafe New Zealand that the premises has recorded risk assessments, safe work procedures, and emergency plans. As the business is pure wholesale distribution and does not perform maintenance or certification release of parts, no Civil Aviation Rule Part 145 certificate is required; however, import and traceability documentation for every certified release part must be maintained for inspection by CAA, Customs, or commercial counterparties.
required_dossiers: Building Warrant of Fitness and Compliance Schedule
Occupancy certificate or authority to occupy the warehouse
Fire Evacuation Scheme approval from FENZ
Hazardous substances location test certificate and NZS 5433 compliance records (if applicable)
Worksafe NZ health and safety risk assessment
Insurance policies for stock in transit and third-party liability
Aircraft parts traceability and airworthiness release document register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FENZ rejects the Fire Evacuation Scheme, revise the emergency plan and evacuation diagrams and resubmit within the specified cure period. If the territorial council identifies the building use as unauthorized, apply for a land use certificate or building consent amendment. If Worksafe NZ identifies unsafe racking or load issues, undertake the required structural load engineering inspection and obtain a certificate of compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local territorial authority or city/district council, Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), Worksafe New Zealand, the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) in respect of aviation parts traceability, and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment as the administrative regulator of the Companies Register
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general industrial operating licence is required under New Zealand law for pure wholesale distribution; the required physical operational permits are the Building Warrant of Fitness issued under the Building Act 2004, the Fire Evacuation Scheme approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and any hazardous substances location approval issued under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996. If the entity undertakes maintenance, repair, or certification of aircraft parts, a Civil Aviation Rule Part 145 Aviation Maintenance Organisation Certificate is required; otherwise it is Not Applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Permitted Activity. A formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is Not Applicable to the wholesale distribution and warehousing of surplus commercial aircraft parts. The use of a standard commercial warehouse for storage, packing, inspection, and dispatch is typically a permitted activity under the district plan. A restricted resource consent may become necessary only if the activity creates significant adverse effects or involves coating, degreasing, waste treatment, fuel storage, or large-scale hazardous substance storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or stack emission thresholds apply to the pure trading activity. If the site operates a wash bay or uses degreasing solvents, any trade wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must comply with the local council trade waste bylaw, with general quantitative limits not exceeding pH 6-10, total suspended solids below 400 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand below 300 mg/L, and no visible oil or grease. VOC emissions from indoor storage cannot exceed occupational exposure standards under the Health and Safety at Work (General Risk and Workplace Management) Regulations 2016. Hazardous substances stored or handled must comply with NZS 5433:2020, and residual quantities of lithium batteries, pressurised canisters, or aviation chemicals must be documented and consigned through an approved waste transporter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and display of the Building Warrant of Fitness and Compliance Schedule are mandatory for the warehouse premises. Fire and Emergency New Zealand must approve the Fire Evacuation Scheme, means of escape, exit width, fire extinguisher placement, emergency lighting, and alarm systems. Structural load inspections must certify that racking and mezzanine storage do not exceed the building design limits. Worksafe New Zealand requires a documented health and safety management system under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including electrical safety, manual handling controls, forklift licensing, hazardous substances controls, incident reporting, and a worker participation system.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online portal: myIR (secure electronic filing and registration portal accessible via www.ird.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine entity category and registration obligations for a foreign-owned New Zealand limited company. Step 2: Incorporate the company with the New Zealand Companies Office (under the Companies Act 1993) and obtain the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) which is automatically issued upon incorporation. Step 3: Register for income tax with Inland Revenue via the myIR portal or through the Companies Office data feed, providing the NZBN, registered office address, director details, and shareholder information; this results in issuance of an IRD number (often the same as the NZBN for companies). Step 4: If the company expects to make taxable supplies above the GST registration threshold, separately apply for GST registration in myIR electing a filing frequency. Step 5: If importing or exporting goods, apply for a Customs Client Code from the New Zealand Customs Service (via the Customs Client/Agent Interactive system) and obtain a Customs registered client identifier. Step 6: For non-resident directors or foreign entities, ensure a local agent or authorized myIR user is appointed under the New Zealand tax administration rules and file any required non-resident land withholding tax or financial product disclosures if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box or formal hybrid mismatch election regime similar to the US; however, limited liability companies are treated as separate taxable entities, and certain qualifying losses or consolidated groups may be recognized through the New Zealand loss grouping and GST group registration regimes subject to statutory conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 for goods and services supplied in New Zealand over a 12-month period; non-resident businesses supplying remote services to New Zealand consumers may be required to register under the goods and services tax (remote services) rules when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000; a lower NZD 50,000 threshold applies for providers of remote services under certain simplified registration criteria.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate a real-time e-invoicing clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping regime. Peppol-based e-invoicing is voluntary and supported by the New Zealand Peppol Authority. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, and records must be retained in accordance with the Tax Administration Act 1994, including sufficient detail for audit; there is no statutory requirement for a government-issued digital prior approval or real-time API clearance for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A New Zealand GST-registered person may zero-rate the supply of goods that are exported from New Zealand if the supplier exports the goods within the time frames and documentary conditions set out in the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including actual removal from New Zealand within 28 days of supply or earlier if required, the supplier retains the goods as trading stock until export, and the goods are not subsequently returned to New Zealand except as permitted; zero-rating also applies to certain internationally supplied services, transport services, and supplies of qualifying remote services to non-residents under defined conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Export Entry) submitted through New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (for goods exceeding export declaration thresholds), including the registered exporter client code
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing physical departure of goods from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the surplus commercial aircraft parts and confirming the sale to an overseas buyer
Evidence of overseas payment or inward remittance such as a bank credit advice, SWIFT wire confirmation, or foreign exchange repatriation record (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and Tax Administration Act 1994, if zero-rating is applied but export documentation is insufficient or the goods do not physically leave New Zealand in time, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 15% GST, with interest and shortfall penalties for an unacceptable tax position or evasion; deliberate misstatements can trigger strict liability criminal penalties of up to NZD 50,000 for the first offense and imprisonment in serious cases, plus an automatic 100% or more shortfall penalty on the unpaid GST; Inland Revenue may reassess and claw back input tax credits claimed on procurement related to the export transaction when zero-rating is denied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully floating, freely convertible currency under a comprehensive external account liberalization framework. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not restrict the conversion of New Zealand dollars for commercial trade or capital account transactions, and there are no comprehensive exchange control regulations analogous to those in emerging markets. Current account payments, including imports of surplus commercial aircraft parts, dividends, management fees, and aircraft maintenance disbursements, may be paid without requiring central bank approval. Capital account inflows and outflows, including shareholder equity injections into NZ_LTD, intercompany loans, and eventual repatriation of sale proceeds, are likewise permitted without surrender requirements or prior authorization. New Zealand's anti-money laundering regime, overseen by the Reserve Bank, the Department of Internal Affairs, and the Financial Markets Authority, focuses on customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting rather than foreign exchange rationing. The practical hurdles for profit remittance are limited to withholding tax obligations under New Zealand domestic tax law, including non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties, and the financial institution's own AML onboarding checks. New Zealand GST of 15% is recoverable through normal tax returns. No currency surrender or haircut is imposed, and the NZD/USD market operates deeply through local and global interbank channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds in offshore or onshore accounts, with no mandatory conversion ratio or compliance timeline. For ISIC 4659 surplus aircraft parts exports, proceeds must be reported through normal customs and Inland Revenue documentation, but the exporter may hold USD proceeds or convert them to NZD at its own discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: New Zealand does not commonly issue elective money-license equivalents for digital EMIs; non-bank financial institutions can be registered as financial service providers and conduct money remittance under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, but they are not licensed to take deposits or issue commercial bank guarantees. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, and similar platforms may offer multi-currency payment accounts to New Zealand entities, but they cannot support documentary credit lifecycles, escrow arrangements for aviation parts, or dedicated trade finance facilities. Feasibility rating for this NZ_LTD surplus aircraft parts distribution roadmap is Low-Medium. Principal trade settlements must be routed through registered New Zealand commercial banks; EMIs may be used only as auxiliary disbursement rails for incidental operating expenses. No offshore EMI can provide equivalent FX hedging, capital verification, or syndicated credit support for cross-border aviation procurement. Legal constraints include NZ AML/CFT licensing for the EMI, sanctions screening obligations, and the absence of a deposit-taking authorization; therefore, an EMI cannot replace a tier-1 domestic commercial bank for escrow or operational treasury purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banking statute does not impose a universal in-branch presence requirement, but registered banks apply a risk-based customer verification standard. The enhanced risk profile of aviation parts trading, combined with escrow account needs, will ordinarily mandate an in-person identity interview at a New Zealand branch for at least one director or senior finance officer. Remote video verification may be accepted for lower-risk structures, but for this jurisdiction and business scope the bank compliance committee will likely require physical presence or remote interactive verification supported by a New Zealand-registered lawyer or chartered accountant who certifies identity and source of funds. Consular proxy opening is not a statutory right and would generally be declined by major NZ banks unless accompanied by a formal attestation from a recognized government authority and additional notarized due diligence documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity created by indirect corporate shareholders, offshore trusts, or nominee directors for the NZ_LTD entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of the NZ Companies Office register extract naming all directors and all shareholders holding 25 percent or more; if an offshore trust is the ultimate owner, provide a signed trustee declaration, notarized trust deed, identity and source-of-wealth questionnaires for settlor and beneficiaries, audited financial statements or an accountant's ownership confirmation letter, and a written explanation of no undisclosed principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Surplus aviation parts pricing outside declared market values, raising trade-based money laundering concerns through over-invoicing or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide third-party independent condition and valuation reports from reputable aviation appraisal bodies, component history files and approved maintenance organization certificates, invoice-line reconciliation to import and export customs entries, bills of lading or airway bills with harmonized system codes, and prior shipping and customs clearance history to demonstrate actual physical movement and commercial realism.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dealings with civil aircraft rotables and avionics that may implicate dual-use export controls, international sanctions, or unauthorized end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full component manifest with serial numbers, Federal Aviation Administration or European Union Aviation Safety Agency certificates of conformity, export control classification assessment under the New Zealand Strategic Goods List and any relevant US ECCN, end-user undertaking or certificate from overseas purchasers, World-Check and Dow Jones sanctions screening results, specially designated nationals checks, and signed anti-bribery and export control warranties from all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source-of-funds and counterparty country mix for a newly formed entity intending to trade high-value aircraft surplus without verifiable historical operating evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a 12-month board-approved treasury forecast, binding purchase contracts or letters of intent, bank references from the remitting institution and beneficiary banks, notarized board resolutions authorizing specific transactions, certified identification documents for all signatories, evidence of beneficial owner income and accumulated savings or documented loan agreements, and a pre-account-opening source-of-wealth declaration independently verified by an NZ chartered accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder loan transfers for NZ_LTD must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire messages from the remitting bank. The wire instruction must clearly state a purpose code such as equity injection, shareholder loan, or capital contribution. New Zealand banks do not require central bank exchange-control permits, but they require source-of-funds declarations, supporting board resolutions, and remittance advices. For statutory capital verification, a New Zealand chartered accountant or auditor will reconcile the received funds against the share allotment ledger and issue a capital verification certificate or certificate of compliance. Non-resident shareholder injections are unconditionally permitted, though ultimate beneficial ownership information must be disclosed for non-resident withholding tax purposes. Funds may be held in NZD or USD, and no mandatory sale into New Zealand dollars is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for surplus civil aircraft parts will primarily clear over three rails: SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments and intercompany disbursements; commercial letters of credit issued by the bank via MT700 or MT707 for larger procurement contracts; and documentary collections for buyer-based settlement where a letter of credit is not required. New Zealand banks route USD and NZD wires through SWIFT with delivery-versus-payment or free-of-payment settlement mechanics, and all correspondent banks must pass OFAC and United Nations sanctions screening. The company should maintain a USD operational account within the NZ bank to reduce costly conversion layers. Exports of aviation parts to sensitive destinations will be screened against the United Nations Sanctions Act 1993, and dual-use or defence-controlled items must carry valid end-user documentation and appropriate export licenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable forward contracts on NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, and NZD/AUD up to 24 months maturity, supported by underlying trade exposure or balance-sheet exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for converting USD-denominated debt or obligations into NZD or USD fixed-floating structures, executed under an ISDA and CSA with a licensed New Zealand bank

FX options in the form of collars, call spreads, or put spreads solely to hedge forecast aviation parts procurement, with no leverage, no naked speculation, and subject to Financial Markets Conduct Act wholesale counterparty exemptions

Non-deliverable forwards are not a permissible hedging rail for New Zealand dollars because the currency is freely deliverable; attempted NDF usage will be treated by the bank as a speculative synthetic transaction requiring strict treasury escalation and is not recommended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (online) to the Registrar of Companies, confirming directors, shareholders, registered office, address for service, and constitutional particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary month rule: due by the last day of the month in which the anniversary of incorporation falls. Example: incorporation on 15 March 2020 makes 31 March of each subsequent year the statutory annual return date; a reminder notice is issued to the registered office not less than 20 working days before that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an automatic statutory late filing fee of NZ$75.00 (approximately US$46.00); if the annual return remains unfiled, the Registrar may issue a warning notice and the company will be struck off the New Zealand Register not sooner than 20 working days after notice under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993. Directors can be prosecuted for continuing default and fined up to NZ$10,000.00.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general-purpose financial statements, directors' statement and independent auditor's report, where the entity is an FMC reporting entity or a large non-FMC reporting entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies; independent audit must be carried out by a licensed auditor under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed within 20 working days after being laid before shareholders, and must be filed with the Registrar with the annual return in the same filing month; for a 31 March balance date, lodging occurs no later than 31 August in the absence of an extension order.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013: maximum fine NZ$50,000.00 plus NZ$1,000.00 per day; directors are personally liable and the Registrar may apply to the High Court for an order requiring filing, or seek removal of the company from the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company income tax return (IR4), financial statement summary (IR10), and related-party or international dealings schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: due by 7 July after the income year end; with a tax agent extension, filing is deferred to 31 March of the following year. For non-standard balance dates, due date is the 7th day of the 7th month following balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: NZ$250.00 for up to 30 days late and NZ$50.00 per extra month up to NZ$1,000.00; late payment penalty on overdue tax: 1% immediately, 4% on day 7, and further monthly 1% increments; use-of-money interest is charged at the current IRD prescribed rate (9.65% per annum). Continued default permits IRD default assessment, criminal prosecution, and recovery proceedings against company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified auditor's report is mandatory for: (1) any FMC reporting entity as defined by the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, including issuers, managed funds, banks, insurers, and non-bank deposit takers, regardless of size; (2) any non-FMC company qualifying as large, meaning total assets at balance date exceed NZ$10,000,000 or total revenue for the accounting period exceeds NZ$20,000,000; (3) a subsidiary whose parent is required to prepare audited consolidated financial statements, unless a unanimous-shareholder audit exemption is lawfully adopted; (4) any overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand that meets the same NZ$10,000,000 asset or NZ$20,000,000 revenue threshold or is not exempt under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. New Zealand does not impose a standalone headcount trigger; an employee count of 50 may increase IRD and AML/CFT risk classification and employer filing obligations, but does not by itself mandate an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB). For publicly accountable and large for-profit entities, the mandatory framework is NZ IFRS, being New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards; entities without public accountability may apply NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); very small non-reporting companies may apply the XRB A1 simple-format reporting framework. The Companies Act 1993 requires financial statements to comply with NZ GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public beneficial-ownership annual return. The annual return requires directors to confirm from the company's own register the exact legal shareholder names, share classes, shareholdings, and addresses as at the annual return date. Under the Companies Act 1993, a share transfer must be registered promptly once lodged, and the register must be updated before the next annual return so the Companies Office statement reflects all completed transfers. For tax purposes, IRD requires identification of shareholders holding 10% or more in the IR10 and related-party schedules. The AML/CFT Act 2009 imposes a continuing obligation on the registered agent and company to collect and verify beneficial ownership information. A 30-day reporting window applies to IRD where a shareholding transfer affects non-resident withholding tax status or the foreign-ownership category; director changes must be notified to the Registrar within 20 working days, and registered-office changes within 10 working days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (including consents and particulars)
Register of Charges and Mortgages (if any security is created)
Statutory Minute Book (board and shareholder minutes)
Register of Debenture Holders (where debentures are issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000 to US$45,000 per annum for a certified independent audit of a trading aviation spares distributor

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (corporate income tax under Income Tax Act 2007)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general free-zone tax holiday. A 15% refundable R&D tax credit applies to qualifying New Zealand R&D expenditure. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely (no fixed expiry) subject to a 49% shareholder continuity test. Imputation credits attach to dividends to avoid double taxation. Certain accelerated depreciation may apply to plant and equipment used in aircraft parts distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; mandatory e-filing through IRD myIR secure portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, with provisional tax instalments usually due three or four times per year depending on balance date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 31 October (seven months after year-end). For non-31 March balance dates, the statutory deadline is the last day of the seventh month following the balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All worldwide taxable income including gross revenue from surplus commercial aircraft parts sales, interest, dividends, foreign-source income, rental, royalties and other business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report total global income because New Zealand-resident companies are taxed on worldwide income. Reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit under New Zealand income tax rules. Recognise revenue in accordance with NZ IFRS 15; include all associated-handling and logistics income; do not net expenses. Foreign-source income must be included and dates/currencies converted to NZD at the exchange rate on the date of income derivation unless a CFC exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All deductions allowable against assessable income, including cost of goods sold, warehousing, freight, insurance, inspection fees, staff costs, rent, interest, administration and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred in deriving assessable income. Disallow capital expenditure, private entertainment, and legal/tax penalties. Deductibility of cross-border payments, especially management fees paid to foreign affiliates, is strictly tested for economic substance and arm‘s-length pricing under the transfer pricing provisions. Payments to non-residents for services must satisfy the source deduction and withholding rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Net income/(loss) before tax loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 minus Box 2. If positive, this is assessable income before applying losses. If negative, this is the net loss before loss carry-forward rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a loss is generated, ensure it is computed on an arm’s-length basis and not artificially boosted by non-deductible or TP-adjusted items. The loss amount will be carried forward only if the 49% shareholder continuity test is satisfied. For tax purposes, any dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder does not affect this calculation, but changes in ultimate ownership by non-residents can break continuity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Tax losses carried forward deducted
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Previous-year tax losses available and claimed in the current year, subject to shareholder continuity and business continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter losses from prior years only if the same group of shareholders has owned at least 49% of the voting shares throughout the current and the loss years. If there has been a foreign takeover or dilution such that continuity is broken, the loss deduction is completely denied. Keep shareholder registers and transfer documents available for IRD audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deducting available tax losses (Box 3 minus Box 4). This is the amount on which the 28% corporate tax is calculated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable income must be a positive number. Understatement due to aggressive transfer pricing, false deductions, or failure to report offshore bank accounts will trigger civil and criminal penalties. If you are claiming foreign tax credits on foreign-source income, ensure the credits are substantiated with tax assessments from the foreign jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Income tax payable at 28% plus imputation adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income calculated at 28%, reduced by provisional tax payments, resident withholding tax withheld, and imputation credits attached to dividends received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax at 28% on Box 5. Then subtract provisional tax already paid and any foreign tax credits claimed (attach appropriate schedules). If the company is to pay a dividend to a non-resident shareholder, the dividend withholding (NRWT) is not deducted here; it is a separate obligation. Ensure the correct imputation credit account balance is shown, as over-crediting triggers penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 incurs a late-filing penalty of NZD 250, with further NZD 250 penalties for each additional month the return remains outstanding. Late payment penalties start at 1% of the unpaid tax and increase by up to 4% per month thereafter. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 range from 20% (lack of reasonable care) to 150% (abusive tax position with knowledge) of the shortfall. Criminal prosecution for knowingly filing false returns or aiding deliberate evasion can result in fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30%. Under most New Zealand DTA treaties the rate is reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for direct shareholders holding at least 25% of voting power, subject to treaty-specific conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the New Zealand paying company must obtain from the non-resident shareholder, before payment, (i) a valid Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) issued by the shareholder‘s home tax authority, (ii) a completed IR290 declaration confirming treaty entitlement, and (iii) a written beneficial ownership statement supported by constitutional documents evidencing direct ownership. The documents must be retained for 10 years. If documentation is incomplete, the paying company must withhold 30% NRWT; the non-resident shareholder may then file an IRD claim for refund under the relevant DTA, attaching the TRC and proof of non-satisfaction of residence in New Zealand. Beneficial ownership is presumed if the shareholder has full rights to use the dividend and is not a pass-through for another person.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest and royalty payments to non-residents is 15%. Under many New Zealand DTAs, arm‘s-length interest is reduced to 10%; royalties (including technical fees for aircraft intellectual property) are generally reduced to 10% or 5% depending on the treaty. An Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may replace NRWT on eligible public issuances of NZ corporate debentures, but internal intercompany loans are not eligible unless specifically approved. To apply treaty rates, the New Zealand company must hold a current TRC and beneficial ownership declaration from the non-resident creditor/royalty owner; failure to do so triggers the full 15% statutory rate and penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 for cross-border related-party goods transactions (e.g., purchase/sale of surplus aircraft rotables and components) or NZD 250,000 for cross-border related-party services, interest, and royalties; groups with consolidated worldwide turnover exceeding NZD 1.14 billion must additionally prepare a Master File and Country-by-Country Report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regime (ESR); however, corporate residence and tax avoidance rules require real commercial substance and management and control in New Zealand. For an aircraft parts distributor, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include certified parts procurement, inventory holding and inspection, order fulfilment, invoicing, supplier/customer contract negotiations, warranty administration, and technical risk management. A bare or shell company without an office, employees, and decision-making capacity in New Zealand will be treated as a sham and the GAAR will recharacterise income. Additionally, aviation parts distribution requires a statutory licence from the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand; operating without one is an independent regulatory offence and undermines tax substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating sales revenue from surplus aircraft parts, maintaining off-book cash accounts, omitting overseas income, or creating fictitious invoices to claim false deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994, ss. 143A and 143B – evasion offence; conviction may result in a fine up to NZD 50,000 and/or up to 5 years‘ imprisonment. Civil shortfall penalties for evasion or abusive tax position under s. 141D can reach 150% of the tax shortfall, plus interest on unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed or authorised false returns can be prosecuted personally; the corporate veil is pierced where the company is a mere facade. Personal assets can be restrained or confiscated under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, a travel ban and immigration blacklisting may be issued by IRD, and imprisonment of up to 5 years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Unsupported Intercompany Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging or paying non-arm‘s-length management fees, excessive royalties, or inflated interest on intercompany loans to shift profits offshore without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; e.g., paying a foreign parent a 15% royalty for brand use when no brand is economically owned in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 Subpart GC – the Commissioner may adjust the transaction to an arm‘s-length price, increasing taxable income. Transfer pricing shortfall penalties under Tax Administration Act 1994 ss. 141B and 141C range from 20% to 150% of the consequent tax shortfall, depending on reasonableness; failure to maintain required TP documentation shifts the burden of proof and incurs record-keeping penalties up to NZD 12,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or permitted the pricing adjustments may be jointly and severally liable for the company’s unpaid tax and penalties; reckless trading under the Companies Act 1993 can lead to asset recovery orders. In extreme cases, making false or misleading TP records is a criminal offence (Crimes Act 1961) with imprisonment up to 7 years, and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on Dividends, Interest or Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders/creditors without deducting the required NRWT, or applying a DTA rate without obtaining the necessary TRC and IR290 beneficial ownership declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 s. 141E – a failure to withhold and pay NRWT results in a civil penalty equal to 100% of the unrecovered tax, plus statutory interest accruing at 7.9% per annum. The unpaid NRWT remains a debt due to the Crown and may be secured against company assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly neglect withholding obligations are personally liable for the unpaid NRWT pursuant to current director penalty provisions; they may also be criminally liable for aiding and abetting tax evasion. Immigration restrictions (including departure prohibition orders) and personal asset seizure orders can be issued, and a director can be imprisoned for up to 5 years for deliberate non-compliance.
